subject: Request: Canary-based SLA mitigation for ACMEHealth deployment
messages:
From: Sierra Delaunay <sierra@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: SLA carveout for canary rollout - launch in two weeks

Hi Neha,

We're planning a phased launch of the ACMEHealth conversational triage flow on 2027-04-25 and have a hard uptime/latency SLA we committed to our customers (99.9% monthly uptime, p95 latency <350ms on our critical route). Before we go live, our legal and ops teams want visibility into how Redwood will handle a staged canary (A/B) rollout that might briefly change latency characteristics.

Specifically: can we get an official exception or mitigation plan that explains
- how automatic fallback/pinning would work if the canary causes regressions,
- whether traffic routed to a pinned stable variant will count towards Redwood's uptime SLOs, and
- what monitoring/alerting hooks we can integrate for immediate rollbacks?

We'd like something formal we can show to our security/compliance team. Also: any impact on pricing/credits if an incident occurs during the canary would be good to understand.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Sierra Delaunay
Product Ops, ACMEHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sierra Delaunay <sierra@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for canary rollout - launch in two weeks

Hi Sierra / Tom,

Thanks for the clear ask — this is exactly the sort of thing we expect at launch, and we can provide a formal canary mitigation plan that meets your compliance needs. High-level proposal below; I attached a draft policy and the SLA-exception form for ACME to sign.

1) Canary plan (proposed)
   - Rollout: 5% traffic to canary cohort for 48 hours, then 25% for a 24-hour ramp if stable.
   - Guardrails (automatic): auto-fallback to pinned stable variant when any of the following are true for a 5-minute sliding window:
     * error rate (5xxs) > 0.5%
     * p95 latency increase > 40% relative to baseline (or absolute p95 > 500ms)
     * request-level anomaly spike as determined by our anomaly detector (linked).
   - Pin behavior: when auto-fallback triggers, we pin the stable variant for 24 hours and open a conditional review window. Manual unpin requires sign-off from Redwood on-call + ACME ops if the pin overlaps a business-critical window.

2) SLA accounting and exception
   - Canary traffic is subject to the same telemetry collection and is included in uptime calculations, but we will log 'canary window' periods in the monthly SLA report and mark them as eligible for a limited carveout per mutually agreed exception (details in the attached form). The carveout is not an automatic SLA credit — it documents a mitigation and the agreed rollback policy; credits are considered under our incident credit policy if the primary stable route's availability is impacted beyond thresholds.

3) Observability & runbooks
   - We will provide per-route token-level latency breakdown, canary-specific alerting, and a lightweight runbook for ACME Ops to trigger immediate traffic cutover manually. Laura will own the runbook review; Rishi will scope any changes to contract language/credits.

Next steps
   - Please review the attached SLO exception form and the canary-policy-draft.md.
   - If that looks reasonable, sign the form and we will schedule a 45-minute runbook review with Laura and our on-call engineer (proposed times: Tue 4/13 or Wed 4/14, 10–12 PT).

I'll also loop in Markus for any product constraints on pin durations.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sierra Delaunay <sierra@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-12 08:22 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for canary rollout - launch in two weeks

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 10:05 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Canary plan (proposed)
>    - Rollout: 5% traffic to canary cohort for 48 hours, then 25% for a 24-hour ramp if stable.

Thanks Neha — proposal looks good. Two clarifying items before we sign:

1) Thresholds — ACME prefers an absolute p95 threshold rather than relative. Can we agree on auto-fallback if p95 >= 450ms sustained for 5 minutes? That gives our ops predictable behavior.
2) Credits — if an auto-fallback is triggered and we record a verified impact to stable-route SLO (i.e., customers saw elevated error/latency beyond our committed SLA), what is Redwood's standard crediting policy during a canary window? We need this in writing for procurement.

If you can add those two lines to the exception form, we can move quickly. We are on a tight launch schedule and would prefer the 24-hour pin as-is but want the ability to request immediate unpin if our monitoring shows external impact.

Thanks — Tom
Director, Platform Engineering, ACMEHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@acmehealth.com>, Sierra Delaunay <sierra@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-13 15:42 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout for canary rollout - launch in two weeks

Tom / Sierra — great, thanks for the feedback. We can accommodate both asks. Updated commitments below and in the attached SLO-exception-form-ACME.pdf:

- Auto-fallback trigger: p95 >= 450ms sustained for a 5-minute window OR error rate (5xx) > 0.5% in the same window.
- Pin duration: default 24 hours after auto-fallback. ACME Ops can request an expedited unpin; expedited unpin requires joint validation from Redwood on-call and ACMEOps (we'll define a 30-minute response SLT in the runbook).
- Credits: if the stable route experiences verified degradation to the committed SLA attributable to Redwood during the canary window, ACME will be eligible for standard incident credits per the contract. The exception form now includes an explicit note that canary windows are logged and reviewed; credits are applied only after verification and mutual agreement of impact.

Action items:
- @Tom/Sierra: please sign and return the attached SLO-exception-form-ACME.pdf.
- @Laura: can you confirm your availability for the runbook review on Tue 4/13 11:00 PT (if that still works) or Wed 4/14 11:00 PT?
- @Rishi: please draft the short contract addendum clause on credits (I copied the language we typically use).

I'll schedule the runbook meeting once the form is returned. Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth launch.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
